title: Wet-spinning-based Molding Process of Gelatin for Tissue Regeneration
protocol: Dissolve 5 g of gelatin powder in 100 mL of double-distilled water to obtain a 5% (w/v) solution concentration.
Stir the mixture slowly at 60 - 70 °C overnight to achieve a completely homogeneous dispersion without any bubbles.
Plug a 26 G x 1/2 inch (0.45 mm x 12 mm) syringe as the solution injector into clear vinyl tubing.
Prepare 100 mL of 99.5% acetone solution in a beaker glass to be used as the coagulation bath.
Run the peristaltic pump machine at 21 rpm (3.25 mL/min).
Let the gelatin solution stand for several seconds in acetone solution before rolling it up.
Take out the gelatin fibers from the acetone solution and immerse them into 2.5% (w/v) of polycaprolactone/dichloromethane (PCL/DCM) solution with a ratio of 1:20 (w/w).
Let the gelatin fibers in the PCL/DCM solution dry overnight under the hood at room temperature.
Use a peripheral venous catheter of 24 G x 3/4 inch as tube mold.
Load the catheter into the gelatin solution and hold it there for 3 seconds.
Load the catheter into the acetone solution and hold it there for 1 minute.
Load the catheter again into the gelatin solution and hold it there for 3 seconds.
Repeat this alternate procedure 20 times.
Take out the catheter from the acetone solution and let it dry at room temperature for 5 minutes.
Gently take out the gelatin tube from the catheter using a hemostat.
Carefully transfer the gelatin tube into a glass Pasteur pipette with an immersion of 2.5% (w/v) PCL/DCM solution.
Let the Pasteur pipette containing the gelatin tube and PCL/DCM solution dry overnight under the hood at room temperature.
Mount a piece of dried gelatin tube on a carbon stub.
Put the sample into the ion sputter coater machine and coat it with gold for 60 seconds.
Observe the morphology by scanning electron microscopy.
Place fat tissues into a Petri dish containing 10 mL transfer solution consisting of 0.1 M PBS, 1% penicillin/streptomycin, and 0.1% glucose.
Cut the tissues into small pieces less than 1 mm² with a scalpel blade.
Transfer the tissues into a 15 mL plastic tube.
Centrifuge at 500 x g for 5 minutes.
Remove the supernatant and incubate the sediment in a plastic tube containing 10 mL of DMEM with 0.1% collagenase at 37 °C for 1 day.
Centrifuge the plastic tube at 500 x g for 5 min, discard the supernatant carefully, and suspend the sediment gently by adding 10 mL of DMEM containing 10% FBS.
Let it stand for 1 day at 37 °C.
Discard the supernatant, add 1 mL of stem cell medium to suspend the sediment, transfer it into a T25 culture flask containing 4 mL of stem cell medium, and let it stand for 3 days at 37 °C.
Discard the supernatant, add 1 mL of 0.25% trypsin-EDTA, and incubate it at 37 °C for 3.5 min to detach the cells from the bottom of the culture flask.
Add 1 mL of FBS, suspend the mixture, and transfer it to a microcentrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the suspension at 500 x g for 3.5 min.
Suspend the sediment with 1 mL of stem cell medium.
Transfer it to the culture flask containing 5 mL of stem cell medium.
Keep it at 37 °C in a humidified atmosphere containing 95% air and 5% CO2.
Change the stem cell medium every 3 days.
Sterilize the gelatin tube with UV light for 2 h.
Immerse it in 75% (v/v) ethanol.
Wash it 2x with stem cell medium to remove residual ethanol.
Remove the medium from the culture flask containing human adipose stem cells (hASCs).
Add 1 mL of 0.25% trypsin-EDTA and incubate at 37 °C in a humidified atmosphere containing 95% air and 5% CO2 for 3.5 min.
Add 1 mL of FBS, suspend the mixture, and transfer it to a microcentrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the microcentrifuge tube at 500 x g for 3.5 min.
Discard the supernatant carefully.
Suspend the sediment with 1 mL of stem cell medium.
Place the gelatin tube in a 6-well plate containing 3 mL of stem cell medium.
Seed 4 x 10^4 hASCs to the tube.
Incubate them for 2 weeks at 37 °C, in a humidified atmosphere containing 95% air and 5% CO2.
Change the stem cell medium every 3 days to provide enough nutrition for cell growth.
Remove the stem cell medium from the well.
Wash the well with PBS.
Fix the tube with cells with 0.1% acetic acid glacial for 30 min at room temperature.
Wash the well 2x with PBS.
Add a surfactant (NP-40, 0.05%) and incubate for 10 min at room temperature.
Wash the well 3x with PBS.
Add 2% normal goat serum and incubate at room temperature for 30 min.
Decant the solution, add primary antibody nestin (neural progenitor cell marker), and incubate overnight at 4 °C.
Wash the well 3x with PBS.
Add secondary antibody donkey anti-mouse-fluorescein isothiocyanate (FITC) and keep the sample in the dark for 2 h.
Wash the well 3x with PBS.
Add 1 mL of Hoechst 33342 to stain the nuclei and incubate for 10 min at room temperature.
Wash the well gently and observe it under a fluorescence microscope.
Induce and maintain anesthesia by an intramuscular injection of tiletamine (25 mg/kg), zolazepam (25 mg/kg), and xylazine (5 mg/kg).
Perform a pain stimulation test by pressing the rat's fingers to confirm the anesthetization.
Shave and clean the skin of the rat’s trapezius area.
Wipe the cleaned area with povidone-iodine lotion.
Cover the rat with sterile surgical drapes.
Gently cut the skin of the rat’s trapezius area with a surgical scissor.
Create a wound of 2 cm.
Place the gelatin tube directly on the layer between the fascia and the muscle.
Close the wound with nylon suture.
Wipe the wound with povidone-iodine solution (100 mg/mL).
Induce the rat via an intramuscular injection of ketoprofen (2.5 mg/kg) and cefazolin (15 mg/kg).
Keep the rat under aseptic conditions for 7 days.
Euthanize the rat via CO2 asphyxiation in accordance with AVMA Guidelines for Euthanasia.
Confirm the death of the rat by toe and tail pinch.
Follow up with chest touching to ensure no heartbeat is present.
Cut the rat gently with a scalpel blade.
Remove the implanted tissue.
Take photos for observation.
